en: Hymns to the Five Protectress Goddesses 1:
Hymn to Mahāpratisarā.
Om, homage to the glorious Mahāpratisarā.
I bow to that Pratisarā, by whose retention of the dhāraṇīs and other qualities the Tathāgatas and others have attained the most exalted reality, which is suchness (tathatā). || 1 ||
In battle, Śakra, bearing the earth as his banner, conquered many Daityas;
I bow to that Pratisarā, the formidable one who bestows victory in combat. || 2 ||
I bow to that Goddess Pratisarā, the bestower of universal sovereignty, by whose power Brahmadatta obtained a kingdom free from all thorns. (3)
I bow to that Pratisarā, who removes the fear of weapons and the like, by whose grace even a devotee who has committed many offenses obtained the authority over the kingdom.
I bow to that Pratisarā, which merchants remember when they have set out from the ocean, and by which they obtain jewels and all afflictions are pacified.
The *Śrīmahāpratisarārakṣādevīstotra* is complete.
2. The *Mahāmantrānusāriṇīstotra*: Om, homage to the glorious Mahāmantrānusāriṇī.
Homage to her who follows the mantra, who grants fearlessness through the empowerment of the Buddhas, who destroys all fear, and who [rescues] those submerged in the ocean of existence. 1.
Salutations to the granter of boons, who follows the mantra; by the mere utterance of her mantra, the six extremely terrible calamities go to their destruction. || 2 ||
No other planets, such as those governed by mantras, afflict the worlds that follow mantras, nor even their beloved ones; homage to her who follows the mantras! (3)
After the recitation of the mantra, the Buddha spoke these verses, by which there shall be well-being everywhere; [these are] the salutations following the mantra. (4)
In this Kali age, which is bereft of Buddhas, one should perform what is beneficial for the world— namely,
that which pacifies the arising of sins and portents, and follows the mantra "Namo."
The *Śrīmahāmantrānusāriṇīstotra* is complete.
3. The *Mahāmāyūrīstotra*. Om. Homage to the illustrious Mahāmāyūrī.
A person may keep a wicked black serpent near them;
I bow to that Māyūrī [Vidyā] by whose power of mantra this is possible. (1)
I bow down to that Māyūrī Dhāraṇī, by means of which Brahmā and the other world-protectors attained their respective offices.
The one of wicked intellect did not seize the golden-hued peacock while it was chanting;
even with his infallible noose he could not catch it—I bow to that Māyūrī. (3)
I bow down to that Goddess Māyūrī, the reviver of the dead, by whose recitation of mantras even withered trees have come back to life.
I bow to that Māyūrī, who, through association with the mantra, causes the great calamities of the wind to be pacified and who eternally bestows enlightenment upon the Buddhas. (5)
The hymn to the protective goddess Śrīmahāmāyūrī is completed.
4. The hymn to the protective goddess Mahāśītavatī.
Om! Homage to Mahāśītavatī.
I pay homage to Śītavatī, by reciting whose dhāraṇī Rāhula attained auspiciousness even when tormented by all the planetary spirits. || 1 ||
I bow to Śītavatī, who brings coolness amidst the heat of sin, who wards off afflictions such as smallpox and other maladies, and who pacifies the sufferings of both cold and heat.
I bow to Śītavatī, the protectress of travelers for a hundred thousand yojanas, who guards them by means of the wearing of mantra-knots and sacred threads. (3)
I bow to Śītavatī, who was formerly uttered by the Sage dwelling in the cremation ground for the purpose of pacifying the afflictions caused by the planets.
I bow to Śītavatī, who pacifies the fear of planetary influences for those afflicted by the planets and bound by the knots of worldly existence. || 5 ||
The *Śrī Mahāśītavatīrakṣādevīstotra* is complete.
5. The *Mahāsāhasrapramardinīstotra*: Om! Homage to the glorious Mahāsāhasrapramardinī!
In this great trichiliocosm,
I bow to her who benefits thousands, who gives birth to thousands of beings, and who crushes thousands of obstacles.
Since there was always a great festival in Vaiśālī even when it was beset by calamities,
I bow to the Thousand-Slayer (Sāhasramardinī), who pacifies great misfortunes.
I bow to her who subdues the Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and Bhūtas of wicked mind,
and who destroys the calamities and misfortunes of those afflicted by evil.
I bow to that Sāhasramardinī, by the recitation of whose dhāraṇī the Lion of the Śākyas was protected from poison—that [poison] smeared with venom. (4)
I bow to the Thousand-Slayer (Sāhasramardinī), who is the medicine mixed with honey that wards off all diseases and restores the dead to life in this world.
The hymn to the protective goddess Śrī Mahāsāhasrapramardinī is complete.
